items.snippet_en: A Facebook post from Cleveland Clinic states that drinking lemon juice or water will not kill COVID-19 or protect against it, and debunks the theory that the virus cannot live in acidic environments.

items.title: Lemon Juice, Tea Does Not Cure COVID-19 in Israel or Anywhere Else
items.snippet_en: FactCheck.org refutes the claim that a blend of sodium bicarbonate and lemon juice eliminates the novel coronavirus, quoting an infectious diseases physician who states there is no data to support this.

items.title: Lemons Coronavirus
items.snippet_en: Snopes.com rates the claim that hot water and lemon can cure or prevent COVID-19 as "False," explaining that while vitamin C is important for immune function, it's not scientifically supported for preventing or curing viral infections.
St. Vincent's Medical Center lists "Sucking a lemon or drinking lemon-infused water can kill COVID-19 viral particles" as a myth, explaining that the body's internal pH cannot be changed this way.

items.publisher: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine
items.snippet_en: The National Academies states that consuming acidic drinks like lemon juice has no effect on coronavirus infections, clarifying it will not destroy viruses or stop their replication, and there's no evidence it boosts immunity.
Hackensack Meridian Health explicitly states there is no evidence that home remedies, including lemon juice, can help prevent or treat COVID-19 infection.
